note: M16.18's device/browser matrix: the platforms the client is certified on, the text surfaces each one exercises, and the reason for anything it does not. Each covered profile is a real engine at a real screen, driven by TestM1618PlatformMatrix through engine/web/test/platform_matrix.test.mjs. This file is a claim, not a run log — the test fails if a profile covered less (or more) than it declares, and the parity report (cmd/zzt-parity) refuses to certify while a skipped profile carries no reason. Touch GAMEPLAY is not certified anywhere here: it is the open gap task M16.18a, and the manifest row mode.mobile-touchplay stays `gap` until it lands. Reading the screenshots in engine/web/test-results: a tall phone page is captured in slices and a `position: fixed` control bar can be drawn once per slice, so the bar may appear at the top of a portrait screenshot as well as at the bottom. Where it really is comes from the measured rects, which the suite asserts are entirely in the bottom half of the viewport.

profiles.label: Chromium desktop 1280x720 @1x
profiles.notes: The beta's stated platform (README: desktop browsers with a keyboard). No native text control is mounted at all here, which is itself asserted: on a pointer-only device the canvas takes the keys.

profiles.label: Chromium touch emulation, portrait 390x844 @3x
profiles.notes: The 80-column screen is 4.88 CSS px per column here, and the whole grid including the sidebar is on it. Rotated to landscape the letterboxed canvas fills the viewport's height and the fixed control bar lands on the bottom seven text rows: gap task M16.18b.

profiles.label: Chromium touch emulation, landscape 844x390 @3x
profiles.notes: Text entry is unaffected — every surface passes — but the on-screen control bar covers rows 18-24 at this shape, which is the bottom of the board and the sidebar's Save/Pause/Quit block. Pinned here so the M16.18b fix shows up as this list going empty.

profiles.label: WebKit (Safari engine) touch emulation, portrait 390x844 @3x
profiles.notes: Playwright's WebKit delivers touch events but reports navigator.maxTouchPoints 0, so this profile certifies the client's OTHER touch gate: MobileTextInputBridge's `touchSeen` fallback, which mounts the native control on the first touch the canvas sees. That is the path a hybrid device with an unreliable maxTouchPoints takes. Real iOS Safari reports 5 and would take the maxTouchPoints path Chromium takes above; the on-screen control bar, decided once at load, is correctly absent here.

profiles.label: Firefox touch emulation, portrait 390x844 @3x
profiles.reason: Playwright cannot emulate touch in Firefox: with hasTouch set the context still reports navigator.maxTouchPoints 0 and exposes no touch events, so a run here would certify a synthetic path no Firefox build produces. Firefox is covered desktop-only above, and both touch gates a Firefox-on-a-touchscreen build could take are certified on the Chromium and WebKit touch profiles.
